gettingStarted:
Welcome to SimplexDM

SimplexDM is a professional desktop application for viewing, analyzing, and managing 3D Tiles (Cesium 3D Tiles) data.

Quick Start

  1. Load a Tileset:
    • Click the Layers button in the toolbar
    • Select Open Tileset from the menu
    • Or drag and drop a tileset.json file onto the viewer
  2. Navigate:
    • Use your mouse to rotate, pan, and zoom
    • See the Navigation tab for detailed controls
  3. Use Tools:
    • Click toolbar buttons to access measurement and analysis tools
    • See the Tools & Features tab for details

Loading a Tileset

File Dialog

Click Layers → Open Tileset → Select your tileset.json file

Drag & Drop

Drag a tileset.json file directly onto the 3D viewer

Path Input

Use Tools Menu → Path Input to enter a file path directly

Interface Overview

Top Navigation Bar

Access Home, Navigation Help, Database, Dashboard, and Help

Primary Toolbar

Quick access to layers, navigation, measurement, and analysis tools

Left Sidebar

Layers & Regions management, search, and filters

Right Sidebar

Display controls, feature manager, and tile inspector

Status Bar

Shows status, coordinates, tile count, and FPS
navigation:
Navigation Controls

Navigate the 3D view using mouse, keyboard, and toolbar controls.

Mouse (Cesium default controller)

Behavior matches typical CesiumJS: rotate with the left button, zoom with the right button or wheel, pan with the middle button (or as configured by the host app).

Left drag
Rotate / orbit the camera around the point of interest.
Right drag
Zoom (drag up/down) or use device-specific zoom gestures.
Middle drag
Pan the view when middle mouse is available.
Wheel
Zoom in and out toward the cursor.

Toolbar navigation (bottom strip)

Layers

Open the layers menu to load tilesets, GIS layers, and control visibility.

Home view

Fly the camera to the saved home / default view for the scene.

Previous / Next view

Step through camera history (like a browser). Disabled when there is no history in that direction.

North & top view

Rotate to north; use Top view for a nadir (overhead) camera.

Coordinate Display

The status bar at the bottom shows:

  • Longitude: Geographic longitude coordinate
  • Latitude: Geographic latitude coordinate
  • Height: Elevation above sea level

Tip: Right-click on the map to copy coordinates in ITM or GEO format.
tools:
Tools & features

Meridian is built on CesiumJS with optional Cesium Ion SDK add-ons (measurement, sensors). Tools share one active “surface” at a time where noted, so panels do not overlap.

Configuration: Scene visualization (transparency, fog, height ramp divisors, etc.) can be tuned under Project.Optional_tools.SceneModes in your tileset JSON or in public/data/config/app-config.json → Project.Optional_tools. Restart or reload config where applicable.

Display modes rail (above the bottom toolbar)

These modes affect rendering. Transparency, white model, height coloring, and thematic map replace each other’s tile styling. Fog and depth map both use atmospheric fog—only one can be active.

Transparency

Applies a semi-transparent style to loaded 3D Tiles. How: toggle on/off. Opacity comes from config (SceneModes.transparency.alpha).

Fog

Atmospheric fog for depth perception. How: toggle. Density/brightness: SceneModes.fog.

White model

Uniform white styling on tilesets (design review). Restores previous styles when turned off.

Slope

Slope visualization via the display-modes pipeline. Requires display-modes support in the build.

Height coloring

Color by elevation (blue→red ramp). Scale: SceneModes.height.heightDivisor (metres).

Depth map (distance)

Stronger fog density for depth emphasis. SceneModes.distance.density.

Direction / aspect

Toggles globe lighting to emphasize directional shading (implementation-specific).

Snow / Clouds

Weather-style overlays when the display-modes manager exposes them.

Orthographic

Switches the camera to an orthographic frustum for plan-style views. Width scales with camera height; factor: SceneModes.ortho.orthoWidthFactor.

Thematic color map

Alternative height-based palette (cyan/magenta). Scale: SceneModes.remapColors.heightDivisor.

Main map toolbar (bottom strip)

Layers

Open the layers menu: load tileset.json, manage GIS layers, visibility. Same entry point as drag-and-drop in many setups.

Home · History · North · Top

Home restores the default view. Previous/Next walk camera history. North aligns heading to north. Top nadir view.

Share location

Share the current camera / place (implementation opens a share UI).

Screenshot

Capture the current viewport (export path depends on host: browser vs Electron).

Street view

Ground-level or street-aligned navigation when data/providers are available.

Flight mode

FPS-style movement: WASD, arrows, Q/E vertical, Shift boost, mouse look, wheel adjusts speed. Esc exits.

Clip with polygon

Define a region to clip or cut the scene (manager workflow).

Split screen

Two synchronized or compared views side by side.

Measure (Ion SDK)

When Ion SDK measurement is attached, the strip opens Cesium-style tools: distance, area, heights, horizontal/vertical distances, component distance, radius (including custom radius/circle on terrain). Pick on the model surface; zoom improves precision. See Cesium Ion Measure.

Line of sight

Two clicks: start and end on the model/terrain. Shows whether the segment is blocked and can expose height offsets in the LOS panel. Exclusive with viewshed/measure strip while active.

Viewshed (view range)

Uses a sensor-style frustum (Ion SDK Sensors when available) to color visible vs occluded regions. Follow on-screen steps to place observer and target. Exclusive with other analysis tools.

Elevation profile

Click points along a path on the terrain/model; double-click to finish. Samples terrain heights and draws a simple profile (min/max summary).

Display modes (special)

Opens the secondary rail for the scene-mode buttons above. Also links to extended display-modes UI when present.

Other entry points (nested toolbar / dashboard)

  • Bookmarks, Search, Models map, Shade analysis, Oblique views, Model upload — opened from the nested tools menu or dashboard where wired; they call the same managers as duplicated toolbar actions would.
  • Coordinate research (sidebar): convert coordinates, fly to location, copy results.
  • Tile inspector / Database / Dashboard — metadata, paths, and JSON inspection.

Measurement accuracy (industry practice)

Cesium / Ion measurements rely on picks on the 3D Tiles surface. Zoom in, ensure the tileset is fully loaded, and click directly on geometry. For critical survey work, validate against known control points.
keyboard:
Keyboard shortcuts

Global shortcuts are limited unless a tool explicitly captures keys. The flight mode tool uses a full FPS-style map.

Flight mode (when enabled)

W S A D Move forward / back / strafe left / strafe right
↑ ↓ ← → Same movement using arrow keys
Q E Move down / up (world vertical)
Shift Hold to boost speed (while moving)
Space Reserved in flight handler (movement stack)
Wheel Adjust flight speed (m/s) when the flight panel is active
Esc Exit flight mode (global listener)

Radius / circle measure (draw cylinder)

Esc Cancel radius picking and clear the temporary graphics

General

Esc Close this Help window when it is focused; also used by tools above
F12 Developer tools (browser / Electron)

Standard Cesium camera control uses the mouse (see Navigation tab). There is no global WASD pan on the map until flight mode is turned on.
troubleshooting:
Troubleshooting

Common issues and solutions to help you get the most out of SimplexDM.

Application Won't Start

Problem: Application window doesn't open or crashes immediately.
Solutions:
  • Check Node.js version (should be 16.0+)
  • Verify dependencies: npm install
  • Check console for errors (F12)
  • Verify CesiumJS is installed in public/lib/cesium/
  • Check if port 8000 is available

Tileset Won't Load

Problem: Tileset fails to load or shows errors.
Solutions:
  • Verify tileset JSON file is valid
  • Check file paths in tileset JSON (relative vs absolute)
  • Ensure all referenced files exist
  • Check server console for 404 errors
  • Verify file permissions
  • Try using absolute paths in tileset JSON

Map Tiles Not Showing

Problem: Base map tiles don't display.
Solutions:
  • Check internet connection (for online tiles)
  • Verify offline tiles exist in data/tiles/
  • Check data/tiles/meta.json for correct zoom levels
  • Verify server is serving from data/ directory
  • Check browser console for CORS or loading errors

Performance Issues

Problem: Application is slow or laggy.
Solutions:
  • Reduce visible layers
  • Lower tile cache size in configuration
  • Use performance monitor to identify bottlenecks
  • Reduce zoom level for large areas
  • Close other applications to free memory
  • Check system requirements (RAM, GPU)

Measurements Inaccurate

Problem: Measurement results are incorrect.
Solutions:
  • Zoom in closer - This is critical for accuracy (10cm precision)
  • Check you're clicking on the model surface
  • Verify measurement tool is active
  • Ensure tileset is fully loaded

Measure toolbar missing or “not ready”

Problem: Ion SDK measurement mixin did not attach or the toolbar stays collapsed.
Solutions:
  • Confirm IonSdkMeasurements.js loads before the app bundle and Cesium is available
  • Wait until the tileset has finished streaming initial tiles
  • Click the Measure map button to expand the strip (GIS-style default is collapsed)

Line of sight / viewshed picks nothing

Problem: Clicks do not register on the model.
Solutions:
  • Ensure viewer.scene.pickPositionSupported is true (depth buffer picks)
  • Zoom to surfaces that have rendered geometry; avoid the sky
  • Turn off conflicting tools that capture the canvas first

Fog / depth map look wrong together

Problem: Atmospheric effect is too strong or toggles fight each other.
Solutions:
  • Only one of Fog and Depth map can be active—they share the same fog settings
  • Tune SceneModes.fog and SceneModes.distance densities in config

Getting More Help
